issues.description: The template file src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java declares a class named AnimalFarm (and contains malformed/duplicated code), while the problem statement and the solution expect a public class named Farm. The mismatch between the filename (Farm.java) and the class name (AnimalFarm), plus the corrupted content in the template, will prevent students from compiling and mapping the expected Farm class from the UML/Main to the provided template.
issues.suggestedFix: Fix the template by renaming the class to Farm and correcting the file contents to match the expected structure (public class Farm { ... }). Remove duplicated/malformed code (extra package declaration inside methods, duplicated class declaration) so that the class declaration matches the filename and the UML/Main usage. Ensure the template provides a Farm class skeleton with the correct method signatures (addAnimal, feedAllAnimals, singFarmSong, getters/setters for animals) to align with the problem statement.
